newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Oil firms urged to apply to advanced techology.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms urged to apply to advanced techology.

text.p: Oil exploration and development companies had to apply advanced technology quickly if they wanted to feature in the next century, Janet Stoner, vice president of Texaco's oil and production division said on Thursday.
The deep waters off Africa's west coast were proving rich in oil and applying proven advanced deep water technology could reduce risk and bring these to rapid fruition, she said.
Speaking at the Africa Upstream 1996 conference, Stoner said Texaco was applying to west Africa seismic and drilling technology proven in the deep waters of the Gulf of Mexico.

"The application of current and emerging technology in west Africa will yield a faster rate of development than was seen in the Gulf...If multiple techniques are applied that development will be even more enhanced," Stoner said.
"The speedy application of that technology is what will define the winners in the next century," she said.
Texaco's objective was to double its earnings by the year 2000, Stoner said. She added that the company's international upstream performance would make a significant contribution.
"Africa has a significant role to play for us there."
Applying new technology would also help to speed up the cycle process (period to bring exploration to first production), which was also crucial to success, Stoner said.

"Looking along the Nigerian coast six out of six wells have been cut and encountered hydrocarbons (at the time of collecting data), obviously more wells have been drilled and eight out of eight is a more recent number," she said.
"With this kind of success it is difficult not to be bullish on the deep waters of the African coast."
Technology being employed includes three-dimensional visualisation, seismic activated analysis and three-dimensional stratigraphy.
"Three-D seismic is no longer an appraisal and development tool but one to be used aggressively in exploration," she said.
Applying such technology as well as horizontal drilling to Nigerian waters had raised Texaco's field production there to 75,000 barrels per day from 58,000 barrels per day.
Stoner called for collaboration to optimise the use of deep water rigs around the world.
